skill.name: backend-atomic-commit
skill.description: Run strict backend pre-commit checks for Django-style repositories, fix safe issues, and prepare atomic commits with clear quality gates.
skill.summary: Validate and prepare backend changes with strict linting, type checks, tests, and atomic commit guidance.
skill.author: DiversioTeam

security_audit.summary: The skill is a documentation-only workflow, but it grants Bash and instructs agents to run repo-local tools, pre-commit hooks, tests, and hidden .security scripts. Most static hits are false positives from markdown backticks; the confirmed risks are bounded external command execution and hidden-script execution in the target workspace.

remediation.issue: Repo-local hidden scripts may be executed during checks.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running .security scripts in unfamiliar repositories, and show the exact script paths before execution.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use command substitution over git output.
remediation.suggestion: Replace command-substitution examples with safer file-list handling that preserves filenames and avoids accidental option parsing.

remediation.issue: The skill can run hooks and tests that execute project code.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should only run the skill in trusted workspaces or after reviewing hook and test commands.

content.value_statement: Backend changes often fail review because formatting, type checks, tests, or commit scope are not ready. This skill runs strict pre-commit workflows and explains what must change before a safe atomic commit.
actual_capabilities: Checks changed and staged files with git status and git diff context.
Runs or recommends Ruff, ty, Django checks, pytest subsets, and pre-commit hooks.
Applies safe formatting, import, typing, logging, and fixture cleanups in pre-commit mode.
Evaluates whether staged changes form one coherent atomic commit.
Proposes ticket-prefixed commit messages without AI signatures or plugin branding.
Reports blocking issues, recommended fixes, and checks that could not run.
limitations: It is tuned for Django and Diversio-style backend repositories, not all languages.
It may execute project-local hooks, tests, and scripts when the user allows commands.
It cannot guarantee commit readiness when dependencies, databases, or test environments are missing.
It does not replace human review for risky migrations or business logic changes.

use_cases.title: Clean a backend working tree
use_cases.description: Run strict formatting, linting, typing, and safety checks before opening a review.

use_cases.title: Validate staged commit scope
use_cases.description: Check whether staged files represent one coherent change and identify blockers before committing.

use_cases.title: Standardize team pre-commit habits
use_cases.description: Apply consistent Django, Ruff, ty, pytest, and repository policy checks across contributors.

prompt_templates.title: Run basic pre-commit cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Run backend-atomic-commit pre-commit on my current backend changes and fix safe formatting or lint issues.

prompt_templates.title: Check staged commit readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use backend-atomic-commit atomic-commit on my staged backend files. Tell me if the commit is ready and list any blocking issues.

prompt_templates.title: Enforce strict Django checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the strict backend workflow for these Django changes, including Ruff, ty, Django checks, relevant pytest subsets, and pre-commit hooks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit atomicity and propose split
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged backend diff for atomicity, identify unrelated changes, run available quality gates, and propose a human commit message only if no blockers remain.

output_examples.input: Run pre-commit cleanup on modified backend files.
output: Summary of files checked and safe fixes applied.
Remaining issues grouped as blocking, should fix, or nit.
List of checks run, skipped checks, and reasons for any skipped checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare an atomic commit for staged Django changes.
output: Verdict that the commit is ready or not ready.
Checks run with pass or fail status.
Proposed ticket-prefixed commit subject when no blocking issues remain.

output_examples.input: Validate a risky migration and related tests.
output: Warnings about destructive schema changes or rollout risk.
Targeted test suggestions and any missing validation steps.

best_practices: Run it after staging the intended files so atomicity checks reflect the real commit.
Review project-local scripts and hooks before allowing them in unfamiliar repositories.
Treat skipped tests or missing environment setup as unresolved commit readiness work.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to hide unrelated changes inside one commit.
Do not bypass failed hooks or tests just to produce a commit message.
Do not run project-local scripts from untrusted repositories without review.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: No. It prepares checks and proposes a commit message, but the user remains responsible for committing.

faq.question: Which repositories fit best?
faq.answer: It fits Django backend repositories with Ruff, ty, pytest, pre-commit, and local policy files.

faq.question: Can it edit files?
faq.answer: Yes, in pre-commit mode it can apply safe formatting, lint, typing, logging, and cleanup changes.

faq.question: Why does it check atomicity?
faq.answer: Atomic commits make review safer by keeping each commit focused on one logical change.

faq.question: Does it add Claude or AI signatures?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly avoids AI signatures and plugin branding in commit messages.

faq.question: Is it safe to run in any repository?
faq.answer: Use caution in untrusted repositories because hooks, tests, and local scripts can execute project code.
